draft.title: The law of demand
card: Demand is the quantity of a good that buyers are willing and able to buy at each price over a period of time.
The law of demand says that as the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls, other things equal. As the price falls, the quantity demanded rises.
A demand curve slopes downward. It shows price on the vertical axis and quantity demanded on the horizontal axis.
A change in the good's own price moves buyers along the same demand curve. The curve itself does not move. Other things equal means that everything else that affects buying is held constant.
draft.remember: A price change moves buyers along the demand curve: higher price, lower quantity demanded.

a.q: Which statement best describes the law of demand?
opts: A higher price lowers the quantity demanded, all else equal
A higher price raises the quantity demanded, all else equal
A higher price lowers the demand for every other good
A higher quantity demanded raises the price, all else equal
a.why: The law links a good's own price to the quantity demanded, and they move in opposite directions. The last option reverses cause and effect, because the law says price changes quantity demanded, not the other way round.
a.clue: Price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions.

b.q: A café in Geelong raises the price of its meat pies from $5 to $6, and no other factor changes. What happens on the demand curve for its pies?
opts: A movement along the curve to a lower quantity demanded
A movement along the curve to a higher quantity demanded
The whole curve shifts to the left
The whole curve shifts to the right
b.why: The pie's own price changed, so buyers move along the same demand curve to a lower quantity demanded. A shift of the whole curve would need a change in something other than the pie's own price.
b.clue: Only the pie's own price changed.

a.best: A higher price lowers the quantity demanded, all else equal

b.best: A movement along the curve to a lower quantity demanded

problems.detail: Why (a) says 'The last option reverses cause and effect', but options are shown in random order. In this order the last option is the correct answer, and the reversed option ('A higher quantity demanded raises the price') is third. The why should name the option by its content, not its position.
